chosen.title: Surveillance Wages: How AI Turned Your Every Keystroke Into a Pay Cut
chosen.rationale: "Surveillance pay" — AI systems that monitor workers in real time and quietly individualize wages downward — has become the summer 2026 flashpoint in labor economics and privacy law, with economists and AGs now naming it directly. It's the cleanest possible Dawn story: surveillance capitalism, data justice, and automation's human cost fused into a single mechanism that follows the money and names who pays.

sources.name: Let's Data Science — AI Workplace Surveillance Raises Legal and Ethical Questions

rejected_candidates.title: The Last Referees: State Attorneys General Are the Only Thing Left Standing Between AI and Its Victims
rejected_candidates.rationale: With Colorado gutting its landmark AI antidiscrimination law under industry pressure (July 2026) and federal enforcement in retreat, a wave of state AGs has become the de facto national regulator of algorithmic harm — a structural power shift happening right now. Dawn owns the 'corporate capture of public institutions' angle: what happens to accountability when the law is repealed and only a patchwork of understaffed state offices is left to enforce it.

sources.name: Quinn Emanuel — When Machines Discriminate: The Rise of AI Bias Lawsuits

rejected_candidates.title: Engineered Precarity: The Global South Workers Who Train AI Under Constant Machine Surveillance
rejected_candidates.rationale: A February 2026 GIZ study drawing on 35+ expert interviews documents how algorithmic management — live-video monitoring, keystroke discipline, zero-tolerance error metrics — governs data workers and content moderators with almost no legal protection outside the Global North. This is Dawn's postcolonial/data-colonialism lane specifically: not the existence of hidden labor, but the surveillance apparatus that disciplines it, and who is excluded from the room where the rules get written.

sources.name: GIZ (2026) — Engineered Precarities: Algorithmic Management in Data Work and Content Moderation
